profile.a: The author as co-lead of a six-person, multicultural Cambridge Venture Project team (names changed), writing for Management Praxis I.
The course assessors; the client was a local charity serving a community with different ethnic and cultural groups.
Five incidents of team friction during the project and how the author changed his leadership to get the team delivering.
Michaelmas term 2024, from the client visit in week 2 to the final week; handed in on 8 January 2025.
Cambridge, with an anonymised local charity (the same client as the CVP presentation).
Four early assumptions proved wrong: the client had a humanitarian rather than business aim, and team motivation varied widely in an unpaid project.
Project funnel, task-group-individual needs, difficult conversations, personality styles, power management, then Trello and Gantt charts, OKRs and 'disagree and commit'.

facts.what: Time taken to discover the client's aim was humanitarian, not commercial
Interview objective set as an OKR
Time taken to run the interviews

charts.title: Interviews: the objective and the result
charts.takeaway: Once the team had a shared plan and owned its tasks, it beat its own target by 50% in under a week. It is the only measured outcome in the report and the evidence that the change in method worked.

charts.title: The five incidents in sequence

items.title: I. Client visit (week 2)
items.text: Some members ask nothing; the team realises the charity's impact on individual lives.

items.title: II. Calling on a quiet member
items.text: A private talk, then an invitation to speak in a group session. Well meant, but some felt she was put on the spot.

items.title: III. 'Not paid to do this'
items.text: In the second-to-last week a member refuses extra work. The co-leads set up a non-judgemental joint session.

items.title: IV. Difficult conversations
items.text: One-to-ones with the resistant member and a power struggle with the co-lead, handled by changing the author's own style.

items.title: V. Taking ownership
items.text: Trello, Gantt charts, OKRs and 'disagree and commit'; 15 interviews in under 7 days.

charts.takeaway: Problems peaked late in the project; the fix was structural (roles, plan, targets) rather than another conversation.

charts.title: The author's assumptions against what happened

items.title: The client wants a business result
items.text: It wanted better community engagement for humanitarian reasons, which left no business KPIs. Took 2 weeks to establish.

items.title: Cambridge peers will be highly committed
items.text: Motivation varied widely; one member openly said he was not paid to do the work.

items.title: The team shares a view of the client's needs
items.text: Several members had never encountered this kind of organisation in their home countries.

items.title: The humanitarian purpose will motivate everyone
items.text: Questionable early on; it took hold only once members owned specific tasks.

charts.takeaway: The report's method is to state assumptions and test them, which turns team problems into things that can be checked.
